- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect momentum decay.  
- If sentiment is mixed or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model often underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2-5% for the next 3-5 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- When true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days), model exhibits lag bias; shift forecast downward by 1-3% for the next 3-7 days to align with recent price action.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to overreact to early recovery; dampen forecast rise in first 2-3 days of rebound.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 10-20% in flat or negative sentiment windows.
